title.narrative: Community perceptions of the ACE Africa program: acceptability, participation, o

description.narrative: ACE works in four rural locations in Siaya, Nyanza Province, Kenya (recent administrative boundary changes enforced this development) where operational research indicates 30% of adults are showing signs and symptoms of AIDS and 43% of children are orphaned. In these remote areas, people lack access to basic services including; medication, nutritious food, shelter, psychosocial support and education. With over 64% of the population living in absolute poverty, communities lack the skills and capacity to cope with the increasing number of OVC. (Ref ACE Africa 2006) In the specific target areas where ACE works, HIV and AIDS interventions mainly focus on PMTCT and HBC and there are no other organisations implementing an OVC programme in the areas where there are approximately 21,000 OVC. Working with over 500 community volunteers ( 80% women and 50% HIV positive) this project will continue to strengthen community structures and skills to care for OVC and PLWA through training in; proposal writing and budgeting, project management and implementation, nutrition based income generating activities and the provision of outreach counselling and testing. In addition, local stakeholders’ participation will be enhanced through strengthening institutional HIV and AIDS work place policies and ultimately fully engaging government, community and other partners in the protection and the promotion of human rights and child welfare at the local and national level. The project will result in improved community health and economic status, increased protection and advocacy for the rights of women and children, decreased stigma associated with HIV and AIDS and a strengthened community led, sustainable orphan support system involving government and local partners.
